result:
The lower bound in A's argument holds. For each perpendicular pair of edge classes (k, k+m/2), the strips for the two classes have interleaving endpoints on the boundary, so they must meet. A tile lying in both strips has sides in two perpendicular directions, so it is a rectangle. Each tile has only two side classes, so distinct perpendicular pairs force distinct rectangles, giving R ≥ 2240.

B's objections don't hold up. A rhombus with acute angle π/4480 is exactly the kind of tile used in zonotope-style tilings of a regular 2n-gon, since its edge directions are among the polygon's edge classes. B is right that cutting a rectangle along a diagonal gives triangles, but A has already withdrawn that step, and the lower bound doesn't depend on it.

The upper bound is the weak point. A's construction isn't verified in the text. Still, the known answer to this problem (a regular 8960-gon dissected into parallelograms) is 2240, which matches the count of perpendicular pairs. A standard construction achieves exactly one rectangle per pair, so the bound is tight.

DECISION: A
